findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile parent AC3: either restate it to measure one-implementation-per-consolidated-construct (which AC1 already enforces) with line count kept advisory, or name which children must delete enough copies to drive the aggregate negative — currently no child delivers a negative net and the measured aggregate is +241.
evidence: Parent AC3: 'The net non-test line count across the consolidation children's landed changes is negative; checked by summing git show --numstat over those children's trailer commits.'

Epic comment (verified): 'AC3 RE-MEASURED at 8 of the consolidation children merged. It is trending FURTHER positive, not converging on negative ... SUBTOTAL add=818 del=577 NET=+241. Only three children are net-negative and none by more than 13 lines.'

Individual child ACs invert the aggregate: 4cee/fit_for_send is described as 'about line-neutral, not net-negative'; 44ff states 'This child is about line-neutral ... the epic's net-negative criterion is a SUM'; da84 records net delta as 'RECORDED (not gated)' rather than gated negative; a73e adds a guard test with no deletions.
findings.finding: Parent AC3 (the net non-test line count across the consolidation children's landed changes is negative) is not covered by the union of children and is contradicted by the children's own deliverables. The consolidation children legitimately produce net-POSITIVE non-test line counts because each extraction relocates a duplicated body into a single documented owner module, and the epic's own recorded measurement shows the aggregate trending positive (+241 across 8 landed children), not negative.
findings.location: parent AC3 vs consolidation children (1cf6, 3436, 4329, 44ff, 4cee, 6f18, 7931, a73e, d6e3, da84, fcb7)
scenarios: Epic close gate sums git show --numstat over consolidation children's trailer commits and finds a positive total, failing AC3 while every child's own guarantee (one implementation per construct) holds.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend AC3 to gate on 'exactly one implementation per consolidated construct' (the guard tests) and demote the line-count to a recorded observation, as the epic's own tracking comment recommends.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Restate parent AC2 to 'no pre-existing test's asserted property changes; a re-pointed reference or removed duplicated helper block is expected and recorded by the child', keeping 'additions only' as a review heuristic rather than the gate.
evidence: Parent AC2: '... checked by git diff --stat origin/main -- tests/ of each landed change showing only additions.'

Epic comment (verified): '25b4 deletes lines across 14 pre-existing test files ... 6f18 deletes 22 lines in its own new test_store_paths.py ... plus -1 in test_compact_trigger.py and -6 in test_enrich_queue.py. ... the enrich_queue edit IS an assertion ... it asserts the SAME property and had no choice.'
25b4's own AC set records deletions of duplicated launch blocks across 14 converted modules as the whole point of the story, which the 'only additions in tests/' proxy cannot satisfy.
findings.finding: Parent AC2's stated CHECK ('git diff --stat origin/main -- tests/ of each landed change showing only additions') is a proxy that at least two consolidation children legitimately violate, so the union does not cover AC2 as written even though its INTENT (no pinned observable behaviour changes) holds. This is a partial-without-remainder / bypass-annotation contradiction: children delete pre-existing test lines and re-point an assertion at the consolidated owner, which the literal criterion forbids.
findings.location: parent AC2 vs children 25b4 (nested pytest) and 6f18 (StorePaths)
scenarios: Epic close runs 'git diff --stat origin/main -- tests/' for 25b4 or 6f18, sees deletions, and the literal AC2 check fails despite no pinned assertion changing its asserted property.
findings.suggested_fix: Adopt the wording the epic's own AC2-tracking comment proposes.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the Approach section's conjunction example to match the working precedent (os.O_CREAT + stamped_file_is_stale, as in stamped_lock.py), since a bare/conjoined O_EXCL over-matches legitimate lines and mis-flags the diagnostic reader.
evidence: Plan Approach: '(for example `os.O_EXCL` together with `stamped_file_is_stale`)'
src/rebar/_store/stamped_lock.py:119 uses `if "os.O_CREAT" not in text or "stamped_file_is_stale" not in text`
stamped_lock.py:114-117 comment: 'a bare O_EXCL scan over-matches seven legitimate lines, and O_EXCL conjoined with the table still flags _commands/doctor_locks.py'
findings.finding: The Approach section's illustrative conjunction example ('os.O_EXCL together with stamped_file_is_stale') names the wrong atom relative to the working precedent it points at: the actual stamped-lock guard anchors on os.O_CREAT + stamped_file_is_stale and its own comment documents that O_EXCL over-matches seven legitimate lines and still mis-flags the diagnostic reader (doctor_locks.py). The mechanism is sound; only the cited atom is inaccurate.
findings.location: Approach section, parenthetical 'for example os.O_EXCL together with stamped_file_is_stale'
scenarios: A consolidation child copying the plan's example to build its own guard picks O_EXCL and inherits the over-matching the codebase already discovered and rejected.
findings.suggested_fix: Change '(for example `os.O_EXCL` together with `stamped_file_is_stale`)' to '(for example `os.O_CREAT` together with `stamped_file_is_stale`, as `_store/stamped_lock.py` anchors)'.

findings.finding: The first acceptance criterion and the Acceptance Criteria preamble both point to 'the fourteen named under Child responsibilities', but no 'Child responsibilities' section appears in the plan; the fourteen consolidation children are never enumerated, so 'each [inventoried duplication] delivered by one consolidation child' cannot be checked against a list.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add the missing 'Child responsibilities' enumeration (or list the consolidation-child IDs inline) and correct the count from fourteen to the actual number, so AC1/AC2/AC3 bind a determinate set of children.
evidence: Parent AC preamble: 'The consolidation children — the fourteen named under "Child responsibilities"'.
The reviewed parent description has no '## Child responsibilities' section; only '## Scope' and '## Acceptance Criteria' appear.
Epic comment (verified): 'the Acceptance Criteria section says the fourteen named under Child responsibilities ... There are now THIRTEEN — ticket 825c was unparented and closed out of scope.'
findings.finding: The parent's AC preamble names 'the fourteen named under Child responsibilities' as the consolidation class, but the reviewed parent description contains NO 'Child responsibilities' section, and the epic's own comment records the count is now THIRTEEN (825c was closed out of scope). The consolidation-vs-hardening class boundary is therefore not resolvable from the plan text alone, which makes AC1/AC2/AC3 (scoped to 'consolidation children') ambiguous about which roster children they bind.
findings.location: parent Acceptance Criteria preamble; affects class assignment of every roster child
scenarios: A reviewer or close gate must decide whether, e.g., a73e (a guard-only child) or 73b8/7e0d (tooling/guard children) count as 'consolidation children' for AC1/AC2/AC3, but the referenced enumeration is absent and the stated count is stale.
findings.suggested_fix: List the consolidation-child ticket IDs explicitly in the AC preamble and drop the reference to the absent section; update the count to reflect 825c's removal.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the title/Context/Approach so the headline intent covers BOTH work classes — consolidating duplicated logic AND the process-hardening children that add behaviour — instead of framing the whole epic as pure consolidation.
evidence: Title: 'Collapse duplicated logic into shared modules (fortnight defect review)'
'The hardening children (...) close the process gaps the same defect review found: they deliberately ADD behaviour and lines, so the two consolidation guarantees do not apply to them'
Approach section describes only 'Each child collapses one duplicated computation into one shared module' with no mention of hardening work
findings.finding: The title and Context/Approach frame the epic purely as collapsing duplicated logic into shared modules, but 9 of the 23 children are 'hardening children' that the plan itself says 'deliberately ADD behaviour and lines' to close process gaps. The headline intent (consolidation, net-negative lines, no behaviour change) does not describe roughly 40% of the work, so a reader taking the title at face value would not expect behaviour-adding children.
findings.location: Title and 'Acceptance Criteria' preamble distinguishing consolidation vs hardening children
scenarios: A reader scanning the title/Approach assumes every child is a net-negative consolidation and is surprised that dormant-fibre-pterosaurs, tireless-ruinable-prairiedog, bold-abeyant-indri, etc. add behaviour and lines.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the Approach section to name the two child classes up front (consolidation vs hardening), mirroring the split already made explicit in the Acceptance Criteria preamble, so the stated intent matches the full body of work.

findings.finding: The a73e child (guard for the outbound-comment fit) has a hard dependency on the already-closed consolidation child 4cee, but the parent plan asserts 'Children are independent'. a73e's guard is meaningless unless 4cee's fit_for_send consolidation is already on main, and a73e was created after 4cee closed specifically to supply the construct-uniqueness guard 4cee's plan omitted — a dependency/ordering relationship the parent's independence claim does not capture.
scenarios: If AC1 for the comment-fit construct is credited to 4cee, it is not delivered (4cee's ACs are behavioural, no guard); the guard lives only in a73e, which presupposes 4cee. A close gate treating children as independent could mis-attribute AC1 coverage.
findings.suggested_fix: Note the a73e→4cee dependency in the parent and clarify that AC1 for the comment-fit construct is satisfied by the a73e guard rather than by 4cee's own (behavioural) ACs.
